claim: Macrostomum lignano is a regeneration-capable flatworm.
source: The regeneration-capable flatworm Macrostomum lignano is a powerful model organism to study the biology of stem cells in vivo.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a defining characteristic of the organism.

claim: Macrostomum lignano is a powerful model organism to study the biology of stem cells in vivo.
source: The regeneration-capable flatworm Macrostomum lignano is a powerful model organism to study the biology of stem cells in vivo.
evidence: This is an assertion made in the abstract about the utility of the organism.

claim: Macrostomum lignano complements the historically used planarian flatworm models, such as Schmidtea mediterranea, as a flatworm amenable to transgenesis.
source: As a flatworm amenable to transgenesis, it complements the historically used planarian flatworm models, such as Schmidtea mediterranea.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work on transgenesis and comparison to established models.

claim: Information on the transcriptome and markers of stem cells in M. lignano is limited.
source: However, information on the transcriptome and markers of stem cells in M. lignano is limited.
evidence: This is stated as the motivation for the study.

claim: A de novo transcriptome assembly of M. lignano was generated.
source: We generated a de novo transcriptome assembly and performed the first comprehensive characterization of gene expression in the proliferating cells of M. lignano, represented by somatic stem cells, called neoblasts, and germline cells.
evidence: This is a primary finding described in the abstract and supported by detailed methods and results.

claim: The first comprehensive characterization of gene expression in the proliferating cells of M. lignano was performed.
source: We generated a de novo transcriptome assembly and performed the first comprehensive characterization of gene expression in the proliferating cells of M. lignano, represented by somatic stem cells, called neoblasts, and germline cells.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by RNA-seq data and differential expression analysis.

claim: Proliferating cells in M. lignano are represented by somatic stem cells, called neoblasts, and germline cells.
source: We generated a de novo transcriptome assembly and performed the first comprehensive characterization of gene expression in the proliferating cells of M. lignano, represented by somatic stem cells, called neoblasts, and germline cells.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about the organism's cell types.

claim: Knockdown of Mlig-ddx39 confirmed its crucial role for the functionality of somatic neoblasts during homeostasis and regeneration.
source: Knockdown of a selected set of neoblast genes, including Mlig-ddx39, Mlig-rrm1, Mlig-rpa3, Mlig-cdk1, and Mlig-h2a, confirmed their crucial role for the functionality of somatic neoblasts during homeostasis and regeneration.
evidence: This is supported by RNAi experiments showing phenotypes affecting homeostasis and regeneration.

claim: Knockdown of Mlig-rrm1 confirmed its crucial role for the functionality of somatic neoblasts during homeostasis and regeneration.
source: Knockdown of a selected set of neoblast genes, including Mlig-ddx39, Mlig-rrm1, Mlig-rpa3, Mlig-cdk1, and Mlig-h2a, confirmed their crucial role for the functionality of somatic neoblasts during homeostasis and regeneration.
evidence: This is supported by RNAi experiments showing phenotypes affecting homeostasis and regeneration.

claim: Knockdown of Mlig-rpa3 confirmed its crucial role for the functionality of somatic neoblasts during homeostasis and regeneration.
source: Knockdown of a selected set of neoblast genes, including Mlig-ddx39, Mlig-rrm1, Mlig-rpa3, Mlig-cdk1, and Mlig-h2a, confirmed their crucial role for the functionality of somatic neoblasts during homeostasis and regeneration.
evidence: This is supported by RNAi experiments showing phenotypes affecting homeostasis and regeneration.

claim: Knockdown of Mlig-cdk1 confirmed its crucial role for the functionality of somatic neoblasts during homeostasis and regeneration.
source: Knockdown of a selected set of neoblast genes, including Mlig-ddx39, Mlig-rrm1, Mlig-rpa3, Mlig-cdk1, and Mlig-h2a, confirmed their crucial role for the functionality of somatic neoblasts during homeostasis and regeneration.
evidence: This is supported by RNAi experiments showing phenotypes affecting homeostasis and regeneration.

claim: Knockdown of Mlig-h2a confirmed its crucial role for the functionality of somatic neoblasts during homeostasis and regeneration.
source: Knockdown of a selected set of neoblast genes, including Mlig-ddx39, Mlig-rrm1, Mlig-rpa3, Mlig-cdk1, and Mlig-h2a, confirmed their crucial role for the functionality of somatic neoblasts during homeostasis and regeneration.
evidence: This is supported by RNAi experiments showing phenotypes affecting homeostasis and regeneration.

claim: Neoblasts form a homogeneous population of small, round cells with a high nuclear/cytoplasmic ratio, which are located in the mesenchyme.
source: Histologically, the neoblasts form a homogeneous population of small, round cells with a high nuclear/cytoplasmic ratio, which are located in the mesenchyme (Ladurner et al., 2000; Baguñà, 2012; Rink, 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous histological studies.

claim: The neoblast population is heterogeneous and includes different types of progenitors and pluripotent stem cells.
source: The recent molecular characterization of neoblasts, however, has demonstrated that the population is heterogeneous and includes different types of progenitors and pluripotent stem cells (Wagner et al., 2011; van Wolfswinkel et al., 2014; Tu et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to recent molecular characterization studies.

claim: Neoblasts are the only proliferating somatic cells which are able to produce all cell types of the worm.
source: Furthermore, it has been shown that neoblasts are the only proliferating somatic cells which are able to produce all cell types of the worm (Morita and Best, 1974; Ladurner et al., 2000; Wagner et al., 2011; Baguñà, 2012; Rink, 2013).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: Neoblasts drive a continuous cell renewal during homeostasis and produce new cells during growth and regeneration.
source: Therefore, neoblasts drive a continuous cell renewal during homeostasis and produce new cells during growth and regeneration (Ladurner et al., 2000; Oviedo et al., 2003; Takeda et al., 2009; González-Estévez et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies on neoblast function.

claim: The most frequently used models for research on all aspects of neoblast biology are the planarians Schmidtea mediterranea and Dugesia japonica.
source: The most frequently used models for research on all aspects of neoblast biology are the planarians Schmidtea mediterranea and Dugesia japonica (Reddien and Sánchez Alvarado, 2004; Shibata et al., 2010; Rink, 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to key papers using these model organisms.

claim: Phylogenetic relations within flatworms and with Xenacoelomorpha are now well understood.
source: Phylogenetic relations within flatworms (Laumer et al., 2015) and with Xenacoelomorpha – the early-branching bilaterians that also have regenerative capacity (Cannon et al., 2016; Hejnol and Pang, 2016), are now well understood, paving way for studies on the neoblast origin and evolution of regeneration (Srivastava et al., 2014; Gehrke and Srivastava, 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to phylogenetic studies.

claim: Xenacoelomorpha are early-branching bilaterians that also have regenerative capacity.
source: Phylogenetic relations within flatworms (Laumer et al., 2015) and with Xenacoelomorpha – the early-branching bilaterians that also have regenerative capacity (Cannon et al., 2016; Hejnol and Pang, 2016), are now well understood, paving way for studies on the neoblast origin and evolution of regeneration (Srivastava et al., 2014; Gehrke and Srivastava, 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to studies on Xenacoelomorpha.

claim: Macrostomum lignano is a basal flatworm (Macrostomorpha).
source: These comparative studies will benefit from additional non-planarian flatworm models, and a basal flatworm Macrostomum lignano (Macrostomorpha), a marine, non-self-fertilizing hermaphrodite (Figure 1A) is being developed as one of such models (Ladurner et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated as a taxonomic classification supported by citation.

claim: Macrostomum lignano is a marine, non-self-fertilizing hermaphrodite.
source: These comparative studies will benefit from additional non-planarian flatworm models, and a basal flatworm Macrostomum lignano (Macrostomorpha), a marine, non-self-fertilizing hermaphrodite (Figure 1A) is being developed as one of such models (Ladurner et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated as a biological characteristic of the organism.

claim: M. lignano animals are small, about 1 mm long, transparent, and easy to culture.
source: The animals are small, about 1 mm long, transparent, and easy to culture, as adults lay about one single-cell egg each day when cultured at 20°C.
evidence: This is stated as an observed characteristic of the organism.

claim: Adult M. lignano lay about one single-cell egg each day when cultured at 20°C.
source: The animals are small, about 1 mm long, transparent, and easy to culture, as adults lay about one single-cell egg each day when cultured at 20°C.
evidence: This is stated as an observed characteristic of the organism's reproduction.

claim: M. lignano worms are able to regenerate missing body parts anteriorly, posteriorly, and laterally, although the presence of the brain and pharynx is obligatory.
source: Worms are able to regenerate missing body parts anteriorly, posteriorly, and laterally, although the presence of the brain and pharynx is obligatory (Egger et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study on regeneration capacity.

claim: The neoblasts in M. lignano are located in two lateral bands, starting from the region of the eyes and merging in the tail plate.
source: The neoblasts are located in two lateral bands, starting from the region of the eyes and merging in the tail plate (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Besides the somatic neoblasts, proliferating cells are also present in the gonads of M. lignano.
source: Besides the somatic neoblasts, proliferating cells are also present in the gonads (Ladurner et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: Several techniques are developed for Macrostomum, including antibody labeling, in situ hybridization (ISH), RNA interference (RNAi), and gene expression analysis.
source: Several techniques are developed for Macrostomum, including antibody labeling, in situ hybridization (ISH), RNA interference (RNAi), and gene expression analysis (Ladurner et al., 2000, 2005; Pfister et al., 2007; De Mulder et al., 2009; Arbore et al., 2015; Plusquin et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous methodological studies.

claim: The first genome and transcriptome assemblies of M. lignano were published.
source: Recently, the first genome and transcriptome assemblies were published (Wasik et al., 2015), and transgenesis utility was demonstrated (Marie-Orleach et al., 2014, 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to the publications.

claim: Transgenesis utility was demonstrated in M. lignano.
source: Recently, the first genome and transcriptome assemblies were published (Wasik et al., 2015), and transgenesis utility was demonstrated (Marie-Orleach et al., 2014, 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to the publications.

claim: The described molecular markers for proliferating cells in M. lignano are limited to piwi and vasa, which are expressed in both somatic neoblasts and proliferating germline cells.
source: Despite this available toolbox, the described molecular markers for proliferating cells in M. lignano are still limited to piwi and vasa, which are expressed in both somatic neoblasts and proliferating germline cells (Pfister et al., 2007, 2008; De Mulder et al., 2009; Zhou et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous marker studies.

claim: There is an urgent need to identify more useful neoblast markers to develop M. lignano as a model for in vivo stem cell biology.
source: Consequently, there is an urgent need to identify more useful neoblast markers to develop this animal as a model for in vivo stem cell biology.
evidence: This is stated as the motivation for the study based on the limited markers available.

claim: More than one billion sequencing reads were generated to produce a comprehensive de novo transcriptome assembly of M. lignano.
source: To produce a comprehensive de novo transcriptome assembly of M. lignano, we made 22 RNA sequencing libraries using different approaches, and generated in total more than one billion sequencing reads.
evidence: This is stated as a description of the sequencing effort.

claim: The data included normalized 454 library, strand-specific polyA-enriched and RiboMinus-depleted Illumina libraries, 5'-enriched RAMPAGE libraries, and 3'-specific CEL-seq libraries.
source: The data included normalized 454 library, strand-specific polyA-enriched and RiboMinus-depleted Illumina libraries, 5'-enriched RAMPAGE libraries (Batut et al., 2013), and 3'-specific CEL-seq libraries (Hashimshony et al., 2012) sequenced using the T-fill method (Wilkening et al., 2013), which allows exact mapping of mRNA polyadenylation sites.
evidence: This is stated as a description of the library types used, with citations to the methods.

claim: The data were assembled using four different de novo transcriptome assemblers, results merged and re-assembled with CAP3.
source: In order to maximize the chances of reconstructing full-length transcripts, the data were assembled using four different de novo transcriptome assemblers, results merged and re-assembled with CAP3, requiring consistent positioning of paired reads (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated as the assembly strategy and shown in the figure.

claim: The set of 60,180 primary transcripts can explain more than 90% of all sequencing reads.
source: The set of 60,180 primary transcripts, which can explain more than 90% of all sequencing reads, was designated as MLRNA150904 transcriptome assembly and used in the subsequent analyses in this study.
evidence: This is stated as a metric of the assembly quality.

claim: The TransRate assembly score for the MLRNA150904 assembly is 0.4367.
source: The TransRate assembly score for the MLRNA150904 assembly is 0.4367 (Table 1, Figure 1—figure supplement 2A), which ranks it as the seventh highest scoring de novo transcriptome assembly out of 155 publicly available transcriptomes analyzed in Smith-Unna et al. (2016) and puts it into the top 5% of transcriptome assemblies by the overall assembly quality score.
evidence: This is stated as a quality metric and shown in the table and figure.

claim: The MLRNA150904 assembly ranks as the seventh highest scoring de novo transcriptome assembly out of 155 publicly available transcriptomes analyzed in Smith-Unna et al. (2016).
source: The TransRate assembly score for the MLRNA150904 assembly is 0.4367 (Table 1, Figure 1—figure supplement 2A), which ranks it as the seventh highest scoring de novo transcriptome assembly out of 155 publicly available transcriptomes analyzed in Smith-Unna et al. (2016) and puts it into the top 5% of transcriptome assemblies by the overall assembly quality score.
evidence: This is stated as a comparative quality assessment based on published analysis.

claim: The MLRNA150904 assembly is in the top 5% of transcriptome assemblies by the overall assembly quality score.
source: The TransRate assembly score for the MLRNA150904 assembly is 0.4367 (Table 1, Figure 1—figure supplement 2A), which ranks it as the seventh highest scoring de novo transcriptome assembly out of 155 publicly available transcriptomes analyzed in Smith-Unna et al. (2016) and puts it into the top 5% of transcriptome assemblies by the overall assembly quality score.
evidence: This is stated as a quality assessment based on comparative analysis.

claim: 51,990 out of 60,180 transcripts, or 86%, are classified by TransRate as 'good'.
source: On the individual level, 51,990 out of 60,180 transcripts, or 86%, are classified by TransRate as 'good' (Table 1, Figure 1—figure supplement 2A, Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: This is stated as a quality metric and shown in the table and figure.

claim: The assembly appears to be complete in terms of genes space, with 247 out of 248 core eukaryotic genes present.
source: The assembly appears to be complete in terms of genes space, with 247 out of 248 core eukaryotic genes (Parra et al., 2009) present (Table 1).
evidence: This is stated as a completeness metric and shown in the table.

claim: BUSCO assessment of the transcriptome using 303 Euakaryotic dataset genes reveals 296 complete, one fragmented and six missing gene models.
source: Benchmarking Universal Single-Copy Orthologs (BUSCO) assessment of the transcriptome (Simão et al., 2015) using 303 Euakaryotic dataset genes reveals 296 complete, one fragmented and six missing gene models (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is stated as a completeness assessment and shown in the figure.

claim: The BUSCO distribution of M. lignano transcriptome is very similar to the assessment of the Schmidtea mediterranea transcriptome assembly Smed_dd_v6.
source: This BUSCO distribution is very similar to the assessment of the Schmidtea mediterranea transcriptome assembly Smed_dd_v6 (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B), which is commonly used in the planarian field (Liu et al., 2013; Wurtzel et al., 2015; Solana et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated as a comparative assessment and shown in the figure.

claim: More than half of the complete gene models are not single-copy but duplicated in the M. lignano transcriptome.
source: However, in contrast to the S. mediterranea transcriptome assembly, more than half of the complete gene models are not single-copy but duplicated in the M. lignano transcriptome (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the BUSCO analysis and shown in the figure.

claim: The presence of multiple copies of genes that usually are single-copy in other organisms can be explained by the observation that M. lignano DV1 line has a duplicated large chromosome, and hence a likely recent partial genome duplication.
source: The presence of multiple copies of the genes that usually are single-copy in other organisms can be explained by the observation that M. lignano DV1 line used for the transcriptome assembly has a duplicated large chromosome, and hence a likely recent partial genome duplication (Zadesenets et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated as an explanation supported by citation to a genomic study.

claim: MLRNA150904 transcriptome assembly has 3503 different PFAM domain annotations.
source: Furthermore, MLRNA150904 transcriptome assembly has 3503 different PFAM domain annotations, 8458 identifiable homologs of human genes, and 1697 homologs of S. mediterranea cell-type-specific genes (Wurtzel et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated as an annotation statistic.

claim: MLRNA150904 transcriptome assembly has 8458 identifiable homologs of human genes.
source: Furthermore, MLRNA150904 transcriptome assembly has 3503 different PFAM domain annotations, 8458 identifiable homologs of human genes, and 1697 homologs of S. mediterranea cell-type-specific genes (Wurtzel et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated as an annotation statistic.

claim: MLRNA150904 transcriptome assembly has 1697 homologs of S. mediterranea cell-type-specific genes.
source: Furthermore, MLRNA150904 transcriptome assembly has 3503 different PFAM domain annotations, 8458 identifiable homologs of human genes, and 1697 homologs of S. mediterranea cell-type-specific genes (Wurtzel et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated as an annotation statistic with citation.

claim: More than 10% of the transcripts appeared to be trans-spliced.
source: More than 10% of the transcripts appeared to be trans-spliced (Table 1).
evidence: This is stated as an observation and shown in the table.

claim: Worms were irradiated with three doses of 70 Gy within 1 day.
source: Worms were irradiated with three doses of 70 Gy within 1 day.
evidence: This is stated as the experimental protocol.

claim: Immediately after the third irradiation pulse, gonads could not be observed.
source: Immediately after the third irradiation pulse, gonads could not be observed.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the irradiation experiment.

claim: From 14 days after irradiation, survival decreased, with 100% mortality reached after 35 days.
source: From 14 days after irradiation, survival decreased, with 100% mortality reached after 35 days (Figure 1—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: This is stated as an observation and shown in the figure.

claim: At 12 and 24 hr post irradiation, no mitotic activity was detected.
source: At 12 and 24 hr post irradiation, no mitotic activity was detected.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from mitotic labeling experiments.

claim: At 72 hr post irradiation, a few labeled cells were observed.
source: At 72 hr, a few labeled cells were observed (Figure 1—figure supplement 3C).
evidence: This is stated as an observation and shown in the figure.

claim: The largest effect on gene expression was observed at 12 hr post-irradiation, with 8929 downregulated transcript clusters (FDR < 0.05), of which 3548 were downregulated by more than twofold.
source: The largest effect was observed at 12 hr post-irradiation, with 8929 downregulated transcript clusters (FDR < 0.05), of which 3548 were downregulated by more than twofold (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is stated as a result from differential expression analysis and shown in the figure.

claim: GO term analysis of the transcripts depleted at the 12 hr time point revealed enrichment for several processes known to be associated with neoblast genes, such as RNA metabolism, DNA replication, cell cycle, and chromatin modification.
source: GO term analysis of the transcripts depleted at the 12 hr time point revealed enrichment for several processes known to be associated with neoblast genes (Rossi et al., 2007; Rink, 2013), such as RNA metabolism, DNA replication, cell cycle, and chromatin modification (Figure 1—source data 3).
evidence: This is stated as a result from GO term analysis with citations to previous work.

claim: Analysis of the distribution of homologs of S. mediterranea cell type markers revealed 105 out of 157 'Neoblast' markers among transcripts depleted at the 12 hr time point.
source: Moreover, analysis of the distribution of homologs of S. mediterranea cell type markers from Wurtzel et al. (2015) revealed 105 out of 157 'Neoblast' markers among transcripts depleted at the 12 hr time point (Figure 2A), which is a 3.3-fold enrichment relative to the expected from random distribution (p<10−15, Pearson's Chi-squared test with Yates' continuity correction).
evidence: This is stated as a result from enrichment analysis with statistical test.

claim: 'Neoblast' was the only cell type enriched among down-regulated transcripts at the 12 hr time point.
source: 'Neoblast' was the only cell type enriched among down-regulated transcripts at the 12 hr time point, and no further enrichments were observed at later time points (Figure 1—source data 4).
evidence: This is stated as a result from cell type enrichment analysis.

claim: Three pulses of 70 Gy within 1 day is a lethal dose killing the proliferating cells, including neoblasts, within 12 hr after irradiation.
source: Taken together, the data shows that three pulses of 70 Gy within 1 day is a lethal dose killing the proliferating cells, including neoblasts, within 12 hr after irradiation.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the irradiation experiments.

claim: A multistep gating strategy based on a live cell Hoechst staining was developed to sort a population of differentiated cells with a 2C DNA content, and a population of proliferating cells in late S, G2, and M-phases with a 4C DNA content.
source: A multistep gating strategy based on a live cell Hoechst staining was developed to sort a population of differentiated cells with a 2C DNA content, and a population of proliferating cells in late S, G2, and M-phases with a 4C DNA content (Figure 1—figure supplement 4A).
evidence: This is stated as the FACS method and shown in the figure.

claim: Irradiation of animals before sorting resulted in a six-fold decrease of the fraction of cells in the 4C gate.
source: Irradiation of animals before sorting resulted in a six-fold decrease of the fraction of cells in the 4C gate (Figure 1—figure supplement 4B), confirming that this gate represents proliferating cells and not contamination of e.g. doublets of differentiated cells.
evidence: This is stated as a validation result and shown in the figure.

claim: By comparing gene expression of the 2C and 4C cell populations of intact adult worms, 7124 transcript clusters were identified as significantly enriched in proliferating cells (S/G2/M cells), of which 5264 were upregulated by more than twofold.
source: By comparing gene expression of the 2C and 4C cell populations of intact adult worms, we established a list of 7124 transcript clusters significantly enriched in proliferating cells (S/G2/M cells), of which 5264 were upregulated by more than twofold (Figure 3A and Figure 1—source data 2).
evidence: This is stated as a result from differential expression analysis and shown in the figure.

claim: The enriched GO terms in the list of genes enriched in S/G2/M cells include nucleic acid metabolic process, RNA processing, DNA replication, chromosome organization, and cell cycle processes.
source: Similar to the irradiation experiments, the enriched GO terms in this list of genes include nucleic acid metabolic process, RNA processing, DNA replication, chromosome organization, and cell cycle processes (Figure 1—source data 3).
evidence: This is stated as a result from GO term analysis.

claim: The Schmidtea 'Neoblast' cell type is the only significantly enriched type in S/G2/M cells (2.68-fold enrichment, p<10−15).
source: Moreover, the Schmidtea 'Neoblast' cell type is again the only significantly enriched type in S/G2/M cells (2.68-fold enrichment, p<10−15), whereas other tissue markers are enriched among transcripts specific for the G1 cell population (Figure 3A and Figure 1—source data 4).
evidence: This is stated as a result from cell type enrichment analysis with statistical test.

claim: 2739 transcript clusters enriched in the germline were identified.
source: For this purpose, genes expressed in late-S/G2/M cells of intact worms (Figure 3A) were compared to genes expressed in late-S/G2/M cells of hatchlings (Figure 3B) and amputated heads (Figure 3C). Since the latter two conditions do not contain gonads, this allows distinguishing proliferating cells of germline and soma, and 2739 transcript clusters enriched in the germline were identified (Figure 3D and Figure 1—source data 2).
evidence: This is stated as a result from comparative analysis and shown in the figure.

claim: The list of germline-enriched genes includes known germline-specific genes, such as macboule and melav.
source: The list includes known germline-specific genes, such as macboule, melav (Sekii et al., 2009; Kuales et al., 2011), and several genes identified in the positional RNA-Seq dataset of M. lignano (Arbore et al., 2015) as gonad-specific (e.g. RNA815_7008, RNA815_9973.1, RNA815_1618.1, RNA815_2640, RNA815_7725.2, RNA815_12337.1).
evidence: This is stated as validation of the germline gene list with citations.

claim: Investigation of expression patterns of 27 candidate genes by in situ hybridization confirmed in all cases their expression in gonads, either in testes or in both testes and ovaries.
source: Investigation of expression patterns of 27 candidate genes by in situ hybridization confirmed in all cases their expression in gonads, either in testes or in both testes and ovaries (Figure 3—figure supplement 1, Figure 3–figure supplement 2 and Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: This is stated as a validation result and shown in the figures.

claim: Knockdown of Mlig-cpeb1 resulted in enlarged testes, less distinct ovaries, and absence of developing eggs.
source: In case of Mlig-cpeb1, the testes were enlarged, ovaries often became less distinct, and developing eggs were absent.
evidence: This is stated as an RNAi phenotype observation.

claim: Knockdown of Mlig-ddx6 resulted in disappearance of both testes and ovaries, and worms obtained a wrinkled appearance.
source: In case of Mlig-ddx6, both testes and ovaries disappeared, and worms obtained a wrinkled appearance.
evidence: This is stated as an RNAi phenotype observation.

claim: When tails were amputated at the eighth day of Mlig-ddx6 treatment, no blastema was formed, resulting in the lack of regeneration.
source: When tails were amputated at the eighth day of treatment, no blastema was formed, resulting in the lack of regeneration (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated as an RNAi phenotype observation and shown in the figure.

claim: 924 transcript clusters were classified as enriched in somatic neoblasts.
source: To elucidate genes enriched in somatic neoblasts, transcripts enriched in sorted proliferating cells of intact worms (Figure 3A), hatchlings (Figure 3E), and amputated heads (Figure 3F) were overlapped, resulting in 956 transcript clusters (Figure 3G). We further filtered this list by excluding germline enriched transcripts (Figure 3D), even though the overlap was minimal and 924 out of 956 transcript clusters remained and were classified as enriched in somatic neoblasts (Figure 3H and Figure 1—source data 2)
evidence: This is stated as a result from overlapping analyses and shown in the figure.

claim: The somatic neoblast list contains 26 S. mediterranea 'Neoblast' marker homologs out of the 157 annotated in the transcriptome, which is a 7.9-fold enrichment (p<10−15) relative to the random distribution.
source: Indeed, this list contains 26 S. mediterranea 'Neoblast' marker homologs out of the 157 annotated in the transcriptome (Figure 1—source data 2), which is a 7.9-fold enrichment (p<10−15) relative to the random distribution (Figure 1—source data 4).
evidence: This is stated as a result from enrichment analysis with statistical test.

claim: 357 transcript clusters enriched in somatic neoblasts were termed Stringent Neoblast candidate genes.
source: To further narrow the list of genes enriched in somatic neoblasts, we overlapped transcript clusters identified as somatic neoblasts by the FACS approach (Figure 3H) with the irradiation-derived list of transcript clusters enriched in proliferating cells (Figure 2C). This resulted in 357 transcript clusters enriched in somatic neoblasts (Figure 3H), which we termed Stringent Neoblast candidate genes (Figure 1—source data 2 and Figure 3—source data 2).
evidence: This is stated as a result from overlapping analyses and shown in the figure.

claim: The Schmidtea 'Neoblast' cell type is highly enriched in the Stringent Neoblast list and contains 22 out of the 157 'Neoblast'-annotated transcripts (17.3-fold enrichment, p<10−15).
source: The previously mentioned GO term enrichments characteristic of neoblast remained in this narrowed down list (Figure 1—source data 1), and, the Schmidtea 'Neoblast' cell type is highly enriched and contains 22 out of the 157 'Neoblast'-annotated transcripts (17.3-fold enrichment, p<10−15, Figure 1—source data 4).
evidence: This is stated as a result from enrichment analysis with statistical test.

claim: 211 out of the 357 Stringent Neoblast transcript clusters have identifiable human homologs representing 159 different human genes.
source: Furthermore, 211 out of the 357 Stringent Neoblast transcript clusters have identifiable human homologs representing 159 different human genes (Figure 1—source data 2).
evidence: This is stated as an annotation result.

claim: Out of the 14 genes tested by RNAi, 5 gave the fast phenotype: Mlig-ddx39, Mlig-rrm1, Mlig-rpa3, Mlig-cdk1, and Mlig-h2a.
source: During the screen, we focused on genes giving fast and robust phenotypes. In other words, phenotypes, which were observed within 3 weeks, in all treated worms, based on morphology. Out of the 14 genes tested, 5 gave the fast phenotype: Mlig-ddx39, Mlig-rrm1, Mlig-rpa3, Mlig-cdk1, and Mlig-h2a (Figure 4A and Figure 3—source data 2).
evidence: This is stated as a result from the RNAi screen and shown in the figure.

claim: The previously described phenotype for Mlig-piwi was confirmed.
source: In addition, the previously described phenotype for Mlig-piwi (De Mulder et al., 2009) was confirmed, and two less severe phenotypes were found: Mlig-pcna and Mlig-cdc20 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated as a validation result with citation and shown in the figure.

claim: Compared to the gfp(RNAi) control intact animals, the number of mitotic cells in intact worms is significantly decreased during RNAi of Mlig-ddx39 (p<0.001, t-test), Mlig-rrm1 (p=0.001, t-test), and Mlig-rpa3 (p=0.048, t-test).
source: Compared to the gfp(RNAi) control intact animals, the number of mitotic cells in intact worms is significantly decreased during RNAi of Mlig-ddx39 (p<0.001, t-test), Mlig-rrm1 (p=0.001, t-test), and Mlig-rpa3 (p=0.048, t-test).
evidence: This is stated as a result from mitotic labeling with statistical tests.

claim: Compared to the gfp(RNAi) control cut worms, there are significantly less mitotic cells for RNAi of Mlig-ddx39 (p<0.001, t-test), Mlig-rrm1 (p<0.001, t-test), Mlig-rpa3 (p<0.001, t-test), Mlig-cdk1 (p<0.001, t-test), and Mlig-h2a (p=0.027).
source: Compared to the gfp(RNAi) control cut worms, there are significantly less mitotic cells for RNAi of Mlig-ddx39 (p<0.001, t-test), Mlig-rrm1 (p<0.001, t-test), Mlig-rpa3 (p<0.001, t-test), Mlig-cdk1 (p<0.001, t-test), and Mlig-h2a (p=0.027).
evidence: This is stated as a result from mitotic labeling with statistical tests.

claim: In case of Mlig-ddx39, less than five mitotic cells per worm are observed in both intact and cut individuals.
source: In case of Mlig-ddx39, less than five mitotic cells per worm are observed in both intact and cut individuals.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from mitotic labeling.

claim: RNAi of Mlig-rrm1 results in a significant decrease of mitotic cells after tail amputation (p=0.008, t-test).
source: RNAi of Mlig-rrm1 even results in a significant decrease of mitotic cells after tail amputation (p=0.008, t-test).
evidence: This is stated as a result from mitotic labeling with statistical test.

claim: In the case of Mlig-h2a(RNAi) and Mlig-piwi(RNAi), amputation of the tail still results in a significantly increased amount of mitotic neoblasts (Mlig-h2a: p=0.001, t-test; Mlig-piwi: p<0.001, t-test).
source: In the case of Mlig-h2a(RNAi) and Mlig-piwi(RNAi), amputation of the tail still results in a significantly increased amount of mitotic neoblasts (Mlig-h2a: p=0.001, t-test; Mlig-piwi: p<0.001, t-test).
evidence: This is stated as a result from mitotic labeling with statistical tests.

claim: Knockdown of Mlig-ddx39 gene proved to be the most severe phenotype of all screened candidates.
source: Knockdown of Mlig-ddx39 gene proved to be the most severe phenotype of all screened candidates.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the RNAi screen.

claim: In situ hybridization performed on adults and juveniles revealed the typical expression pattern of a gene enriched in proliferating cells for Mlig-ddx39.
source: In situ hybridization performed on adults and juveniles revealed the typical expression pattern of a gene enriched in proliferating cells (Figure 5A), known from the published expression of piwi (De Mulder et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated as a result from ISH and shown in the figure.

claim: Both Mlig-ddx39 and Mlig-piwi1 are expressed in the testes, ovaries, developing eggs and the somatic neoblasts, visualized by bilateral bands.
source: Both genes are expressed in the testes, ovaries, developing eggs and the somatic neoblasts, visualized by bilateral bands (Figure 5A,B).
evidence: This is stated as a result from ISH and shown in the figure.

claim: In situ hybridization 12 hr post-amputation confirmed the expression of Mlig-ddx39 and Mlig-piwi1 in the blastema region.
source: In situ hybridization 12 hr post-amputation confirmed the expression of Mlig-ddx39 and Mlig-piwi1 in the blastema region, which consists of proliferating neoblasts (Figure 5C,D).
evidence: This is stated as a result from ISH and shown in the figure.

claim: A combined Mlig-ddx39 FISH / Macpiwi1 antibody labeling revealed cells co-expressing Mlig-ddx39 and Macpiwi1 in the testes, ovaries and somatic neoblasts.
source: A combined Mlig-ddx39 FISH / Macpiwi1 antibody labeling revealed cells co-expressing Mlig-ddx39 and Macpiwi1 in the testes, ovaries and somatic neoblasts (Figure 5E–G).
evidence: This is stated as a result from FISH and shown in the figure.

claim: A combined Mlig-ddx39 FISH/phospho-histone H3 antibody mitotic labeling revealed expression of Mlig-ddx39 in the proliferating cells of blastema.
source: Furthermore, a combined Mlig-ddx39 FISH/phospho-histone H3 antibody mitotic labeling revealed expression of Mlig-ddx39 in the proliferating cells of blastema (Figure 5H).
evidence: This is stated as a result from FISH and shown in the figure.

claim: Many of the M. lignano transcripts identified as enriched in proliferating cells by the irradiation approach have homologs within the set of X1 neoblast transcripts in Schmidtea.
source: Many of the M. lignano transcripts identified as enriched in proliferating cells by the irradiation approach have homologs within the set of X1 neoblast transcripts in Schmidtea (Figure 1—figure supplement 5A,C), and the overlap is 3.78-fold higher than expected from random distribution (Figure 1—source data 4), suggesting the presence of the subset of genes with conserved neoblast function in flatworms.
evidence: This is stated as a result from comparative analysis and shown in the figure.

claim: The overlap between M. lignano neoblast genes and Schmidtea X1 genes is 3.78-fold higher than expected from random distribution.
source: Many of the M. lignano transcripts identified as enriched in proliferating cells by the irradiation approach have homologs within the set of X1 neoblast transcripts in Schmidtea (Figure 1—figure supplement 5A,C), and the overlap is 3.78-fold higher than expected from random distribution (Figure 1—source data 4), suggesting the presence of the subset of genes with conserved neoblast function in flatworms.
evidence: This is stated as a result from enrichment analysis.

claim: There is a substantial overlap between Macrostomum neoblast and irradiation categories and mammalian pluripotency maintenance genes.
source: Furthermore, comparison with mammalian genes known to be involved in pluripotency (Tang et al., 2010) shows results similar to those previously reported for Schmidtea (Onal et al., 2012), with a substantial overlap between Macrostomum neoblast and irradiation categories and mammalian pluripotency maintenance genes (Figure 1—figure supplement 5D), which are 4.08-fold overrepresented in the stringent neoblast category (Figure 1—source data 4).
evidence: This is stated as a result from comparative analysis with citations and shown in the figure.

claim: Mammalian pluripotency maintenance genes are 4.08-fold overrepresented in the stringent neoblast category.
source: Furthermore, comparison with mammalian genes known to be involved in pluripotency (Tang et al., 2010) shows results similar to those previously reported for Schmidtea (Onal et al., 2012), with a substantial overlap between Macrostomum neoblast and irradiation categories and mammalian pluripotency maintenance genes (Figure 1—figure supplement 5D), which are 4.08-fold overrepresented in the stringent neoblast category (Figure 1—source data 4).
evidence: This is stated as a result from enrichment analysis.

claim: Pluripotency repressor genes are nearly completely excluded from the neoblast category.
source: At the same time, pluripotency repressor genes are nearly completely excluded from the neoblast category (Figure 1—source data 4).
evidence: This is stated as a result from enrichment analysis.

claim: The transcripts which are enriched in the proliferating germline cells of M. lignano only show a small overlap with known regulators of germ cell development in S. mediterranea and genes which are enriched in or specific for the sexual strain compared to the asexual strain of S. mediterranea.
source: The transcripts which are enriched in the proliferating germline cells of M. lignano only show a small overlap with known regulators of germ cell development in S. mediterranea and genes which are enriched in or specific for the sexual strain compared to the asexual strain of S. mediterranea (Figure 1—figure supplement 5D).
evidence: This is stated as a result from comparative analysis and shown in the figure.

claim: The planarian germline set is based primarily on the differentiated cells, while the Macrostomum set is enriched for genes expressed in proliferating germline cells, which explains the minimal overlap between these sets.
source: The planarian germline set is based primarily on the differentiated cells, while the Macrostomum set is enriched for genes expressed in proliferating germline cells, which explains the minimal overlap between these sets.
evidence: This is stated as an explanation for the observed difference.

claim: Both irradiation and FACS techniques proved to be efficient in determining the gene expression profile of planarian neoblasts.
source: Both techniques proved to be efficient in determining the gene expression profile of planarian neoblasts (Reddien and Sánchez Alvarado, 2004; Hayashi et al., 2006; Rossi et al., 2007; Eisenhoffer et al., 2008; Blythe et al., 2010; Galloni, 2012; Shibata et al., 2012; Solana et al., 2012) and were, therefore, our first choice.
evidence: This is stated with citations to previous studies using these methods.

claim: The results of the three doses of 70 Gy within 1 day method on the level of morphology, mortality, and decreasing number of proliferating cells are very similar to the previously described fractionated protocol performing several doses distributed over 9 days and accumulating in 210 Gy.
source: This differs from the published lethal fractionated protocol performing several doses distributed over 9 days and accumulating in 210 Gy (De Mulder et al., 2010). However, the results of both methods on the level of morphology, mortality, and decreasing number of proliferating cells are very similar.
evidence: This is stated as a comparison to a previous method with citation.

claim: The effect of irradiation on gene expression is fast and mainly takes place within the first 12 hr after the last irradiation pulse.
source: The effect of irradiation on gene expression is fast and mainly takes place within the first 12 hr after the last irradiation pulse (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is stated as a result from temporal gene expression analysis and shown in the figure.

claim: Irradiation causes a broad stress reaction to the cells, triggered by global DNA damage, but also includes changes due to neoblast elimination.
source: It was shown before that irradiation causes a broad stress reaction to the cells, triggered by global DNA damage, but also includes changes due to neoblast elimination (Eisenhoffer et al., 2008; Solana et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated with citations to previous studies.

claim: Hoechst labeling has been commonly used to isolate proliferating cells in planarians.
source: Hoechst labeling has been commonly used to isolate proliferating cells in planarians (Hayashi et al., 2006; Higuchi et al., 2007; Eisenhoffer et al., 2008; Shibata et al., 2012), and the 4C DNA content is one of the main characteristics of the X1 cells, which are highly enriched in neoblasts (Hayashi et al., 2006).
evidence: This is stated with citations to previous studies.

claim: The 4C DNA content is one of the main characteristics of the X1 cells, which are highly enriched in neoblasts.
source: Hoechst labeling has been commonly used to isolate proliferating cells in planarians (Hayashi et al., 2006; Higuchi et al., 2007; Eisenhoffer et al., 2008; Shibata et al., 2012), and the 4C DNA content is one of the main characteristics of the X1 cells, which are highly enriched in neoblasts (Hayashi et al., 2006).
evidence: This is stated with citation to a previous study.

claim: 6.5% of all cells in M. lignano are neoblasts.
source: This population is much smaller than the 2C population, as 'only' 6.5% of all cells in M. lignano are neoblasts (Bode et al., 2006).
evidence: This is stated with citation to a previous study.

claim: The FACS strategy has limitations, which is mainly the focus on actively dividing cells.
source: As all approaches, the FACS strategy has its own limitations, which is mainly the focus on actively dividing cells.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of the method.

claim: Genes specific for the small population of quiescent neoblasts will be missed by the FACS approach.
source: Consequently, genes specific for the small population of quiescent neoblasts (Verdoodt et al., 2012) will be missed.
evidence: This is stated as a consequence of the FACS limitation with citation.

claim: About half of the identified transcript clusters are specific for the used method (irradiation or FACS).
source: The bias is further shown by the fact that about half of the identified transcript clusters are specific for the used method.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from comparing the two methods.

claim: 3374 transcript clusters are identified with both irradiation and FACS approaches and represent a trustworthy selection of genes enriched in proliferating cells.
source: The other half (3374 transcript clusters) are identified with both approaches and represent a trustworthy selection of genes enriched in proliferating cells.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from comparing the two methods.

claim: Much more transcript clusters are enriched in the germline (2739) than in the somatic neoblasts (956).
source: Interestingly, much more transcript clusters are enriched in the germline (2739) than in the somatic neoblasts (956).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the analysis.

claim: The majority of genes enriched in the germline seem to be specific for the testes.
source: In situ hybridization experiments show that the majority of genes enriched in the germline seem to be specific for the testes (Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: This is stated as a result from ISH experiments.

claim: The large amount of testes-specific genes reflects the functional complexity of the testes and the requirement of producing highly elaborate sperm.
source: It has been suggested that the large amount of testes-specific genes reflects the functional complexity of the testes and the requirement of producing highly elaborate sperm (Arbore et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated as a suggested explanation with citation.

claim: The small overlap between M. lignano germline genes and planarian germline genes can be explained by the difference between proliferating and differentiated germline cells.
source: When considering genes regulating the development, regeneration, and maintenance of gonads and gametes, it is important to distinguish between the proliferating and differentiated germline cells. This can explain the small overlap between the transcripts enriched in the proliferating germline cells of M. lignano and the published datasets of Schmidtea germline genes, which primarily include transcripts specific for differentiated germline cells.
evidence: This is stated as an explanation for the observed difference.

claim: Despite the enrichment in somatic neoblasts, genes enriched in somatic neoblasts are also expressed in the gonads.
source: In situ hybridization (ISH) of transcripts enriched in somatic neoblasts showed that, despite the enrichment, these genes are also expressed in the gonads.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from ISH experiments.

claim: Due to limitations of the ISH technique to visualize single neoblasts scattered in the mesenchyme, expression in the gonads is more obvious than expression in the somatic neoblasts.
source: Due to limitations of the ISH technique to visualize single neoblasts scattered in the mesenchyme, expression in the gonads is more obvious than expression in the somatic neoblasts (Figure 5).
evidence: This is stated as a technical limitation.

claim: It is important to develop more sensitive methods for visualizing gene expression in single cells in M. lignano.
source: Therefore, it is important to develop more sensitive methods for visualizing gene expression in single cells in M. lignano, as this will be essential to confirm the specificity of genes for the somatic neoblasts or the germline.
evidence: This is stated as a need for future work.

claim: It is unclear whether genes specifically expressed in somatic neoblasts of M. lignano do not exist or cannot be identified yet due to technical limitations.
source: The current lack of genes specifically expressed in somatic neoblasts of M. lignano is fascinating, and it is unclear whether they do not exist and neoblasts residing in mesenchyme and in gonads are largely similar, or cannot be identified yet due to technical limitations.
evidence: This is stated as an open question.

claim: Homologues of ribonucleotide reductase M1 (RRM1), replication protein A3 (RPA3), cyclin-dependent kinase 1 (CDK1), proliferating cell nuclear antigen (PCNA), and cell division cycle protein 20 (CDC20) are encoding proteins previously linked to cell cycle processes.
source: Homologues of ribonucleotide reductase M1 (RRM1), replication protein A3 (RPA3), cyclin-dependent kinase 1 (CDK1), proliferating cell nuclear antigen (PCNA), and cell division cycle protein 20 (CDC20) are encoding proteins previously linked to cell cycle processes (Lee and Nurse, 1987; Travali et al., 1989; Henricksen et al., 1994; Parker et al., 1995; Weinstein, 1997).
evidence: This is stated with citations to previous studies on these proteins.

claim: Histone family member A (H2A) was shown to be important for packaging DNA into chromatin and is consequently involved in gene expression regulation.
source: Histone family member A (H2A) was shown to be important for packaging DNA into chromatin and is consequently involved in gene expression regulation (Mariño-Ramírez et al., 2006).
evidence: This is stated with citation to a previous study.

claim: DEAD box polypeptide 39 (DDX39) was not previously studied in the context of in vivo stem cell functionality.
source: To our knowledge, DEAD box polypeptide 39 (DDX39) was not previously studied in the context of in vivo stem cell functionality.
evidence: This is stated as a novel finding.

claim: All five robust RNAi phenotypes suggest problems with cell turnover during both homeostasis and regeneration.
source: All five robust phenotypes suggest problems with cell turnover during both homeostasis and regeneration.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the RNAi phenotypes.

claim: Knockdown of Mlig-ddx39 resulted in the death of all worms within 3 weeks.
source: In case of the DDX39 homologue, all treated worms died within 3 weeks.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the RNAi experiment.

claim: The regeneration phenotype of Mlig-piwi is less severe than that of the other five genes, as a small blastema can be observed in several worms.
source: The regeneration phenotype is, however, less severe than that of the other five genes, as a small blastema can be observed in several worms.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the RNAi experiment.

claim: The Mlig-cdc20(RNAi) phenotype is limited within the first 3 weeks of treatment as the only effect is the disintegration of gonads, and defects in regeneration are not observed.
source: The Mlig-cdc20(RNAi) phenotype is limited within the first 3 weeks of treatment as the only effect is the disintegration of gonads, and defects in regeneration are not observed (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the RNAi experiment and shown in the figure.

claim: Mitotic labeling revealed that already during the 10th day of Mlig-ddx39 treatment almost no mitotic cells can be observed in both cut and intact animals.
source: The mitotic labeling revealed that already during the 10th day of treatment almost no mitotic cells can be observed in both cut and intact Mlig-ddx39(RNAi) animals, suggesting the fast elimination of proliferating cells.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from mitotic labeling.

claim: Mlig-ddx39 is proposed as a positive control for RNAi experiments in M. lignano.
source: Based on these results, we propose the use of Mlig-ddx39 as a positive control for RNAi experiments in M. lignano, which is already a common practice in our laboratory.
evidence: This is stated as a proposal based on the RNAi results.

claim: Mlig-ddx39 could be a convenient marker for proliferating cells.
source: In addition, the ISH results showing enriched expression in the gonads and in somatic neoblasts in both the intact body and in the blastema indicate that Mlig-ddx39 could be a convenient marker for proliferating cells.
evidence: This is stated as a proposal based on the ISH results.

claim: ddx39 is highly conserved in different species, as all members of the DEAD box RNA helicase family.
source: Interestingly, ddx39 is highly conserved in different species, as all members of the DEAD box RNA helicase family.
evidence: This is stated as a known characteristic of the gene family.

claim: DEAD box RNA helicase family genes include a common D-E-A-D (Asp-Glu-Ala-Asp) motive and are known for their roles in RNA metabolism.
source: These genes include a common D-E-A-D (Asp-Glu-Ala-Asp) motive and are known for their roles in RNA metabolism (Linder and Jankowsky, 2011).
evidence: This is stated with citation to a previous study.

claim: Functions of ddx39 have been linked to mRNA export, which was demonstrated in D. melanogaster and C. elegans.
source: Functions of ddx39 have been linked to mRNA export, which was demonstrated in D. melanogaster (Eberl et al., 1997) and C. elegans (MacMorris et al., 2003).
evidence: This is stated with citations to previous studies.

claim: ddx39 was shown to be important for regeneration and development of limbs in X. laevis.
source: Moreover, ddx39 was shown to be important for regeneration and development of limbs in X. laevis (Wilson et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated with citation to a previous study.

claim: An online interface to the generated datasets is available at http://neoblast.macgenome.org.
source: To increase the accessibility of the generated datasets, we developed an online interface to this resource, which is available at http://neoblast.macgenome.org.
evidence: This is stated as a resource provided by the study.

claim: The de novo M. lignano transcriptome and generated sets of genes enriched in the germline and somatic neoblasts are valuable resources for further development of this species as a model organism for stem cell research.
source: In summary, the de novo M. lignano transcriptome and generated sets of genes enriched in the germline and somatic neoblasts are valuable resources for further development of this species as a model organism for stem cell research.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion of the study.

claim: A preliminary screen identified several novel, not previously implicated in stem cell biology, genes essential for neoblast functionality.
source: A preliminary screen already identified several novel, not previously implicated in stem cell biology, genes essential for neoblast functionality.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the RNAi screen.

claim: ddx39 is suggested as a positive control for RNAi experiments and a marker for proliferating cells.
source: Specifically, ddx39 is suggested as a positive control for RNAi experiments and a marker for proliferating cells.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion and recommendation from the study.
